MapleBench

An AI agent benchmark on MapleStory gameplay

Code How agents play Results

MapleBench evaluates AI agents in a persistent MapleStory world. Models receive game state, write a program, and play through a client SDK. The task: gain experience, stay alive, and leave behind progress that remains saved after logout.

Watch the decisions play out in real client recordings, then inspect the results. This published snapshot contains — models, — recordings, and — attempts. Every exported attempt is retained. It is an experiment in progress, not a model ranking.

The quest

Gain experience. Stay alive. Save your progress.

One world per worker.

The cloud rollout moved experiments into separate Linux machines, each with its own rendered client, game server, database, and bounded execution environment.

Scale the environment

Each worker owns the whole game stack. Experiments can be placed on separate hosts without sharing a database, browser, or world lock. Trials within each worker remain bounded and serialized.

Keep comparisons defensible

A class/model cohort stays on one host with frozen inputs. Equivalent VM sizes do not establish equivalent live scenes. The live catalog has 12 completed pilots across Hero, Bowmaster, and Ice/Lightning; Night Lord has no completed public cohort.

Rollout facts checked September 12, 2026. Bootstrap still requires operator-owned runtime wiring and native qualification.

Game state, not a video feed.

The model receives the character’s position, HP, MP, XP, level, map, and nearby monster positions. Journey WASM provides the client observations; the recording is for people to inspect.

Observation and control details Read the technical walkthrough

What the agent receives

HPMPEXP

The model gets the task, SDK instructions, and fresh structured observations: character position, HP/MP, XP, level, map, whether the character is alive, and nearby monster positions. The recordings shown here are for us to watch; this adapter does not send gameplay video to the model.

What the agent can do

The returned program calls sdk.observe(), sdk.pressKeys(), and sdk.wait(). It can move, jump, attack, buff, and use potions through normal key bindings. The mapped class skills may include normal in-game Teleport. The program cannot edit character stats or directly award itself XP.

Where the loop happens

One OpenAI request produces the program. That program runs in a bounded, networkless Node.js container using Docker, repeatedly reading fresh observations and sending inputs through the trusted controller.

What makes it a world

Journey WASM / MapleStory WASM runs the client in a browser. Its WebSocket-to-TCP proxy connects to Cosmic, the open-source v83 server. A separate read-only asset service supplies the client’s game assets. Cosmic handles the game world and saves character progress in MySQL after logout.

Inside an agent’s programIllustrative SDK example
const state = await sdk.observe();
if (state.character.hp < state.character.maxHp / 2) {
  await sdk.pressKeys(['HP_POTION'], 100);
}
await sdk.pressKeys(['LEFT'], 300);
await sdk.pressKeys(['PRIMARY_SKILL'], 650);

Client observations guide the next action. Only the saved server state determines the final XP score.

Built on the work of the community

These experiments depend on nmnsnv’s MapleStory WASM, Cosmic, and the Cosmic bot fork. Maplewright informed the earlier observer work; it is separate from the Journey client used in these recordings. RuneBench inspired this benchmark and its presentation. Explore the projects, star them, and contribute improvements upstream.

    Methodology & limitations

    Scoring progress

    The score is the change in persisted XP after ordinary logout. It includes penalties. Live XP is diagnostic and is kept separate from the saved result. A missing verified score is shown as missing, never silently turned into zero.

    Strategy discovery is the research goal

    Given the same starting conditions, tools, and time budget, how effectively does an agent discover a training strategy? The intended 30-minute benchmark measures the best normalized XP/min in complete 15-second authoritative windows. These five-minute pilots report saved net XP; their endpoints cannot reconstruct a peak rate. Native scoring and expanded skill toolkits are implemented in source and still need runtime qualification. Read the research framing.

    Reading these results

    This is a development benchmark with a small number of attempts. Frozen-input groups share a baseline, scenario, budgets, and runtime settings. They do not establish identical live scenes or statistical significance. Publication evidence is checked separately from the persisted score.

    Learning from the whole run

    An agent may gain XP, execute inputs without gaining XP, or exit without sending any inputs. The recordings make those differences inspectable. Failed and recovered attempts stay in the history even when no score can be verified.
